---
title: "Accessibility statement"
---

This statement applies to the Computing with AI course site, the reading copy of
the material for the joint module between Southwest Jiaotong University and the
University of Leeds. It was prepared and last reviewed on 25 November 2026.

We want everyone on the module to be able to use this site. We aim to meet the
Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, WCAG 2.2, level AA. The UK Public Sector
Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) Accessibility Regulations 2018
require the standard set out in EN 301 549, which references WCAG 2.1 level AA;
2.2 is the later version of the same guidelines, and we aim at it rather than at
the minimum.

## What you can expect

- Every page states its language, and passages in Chinese are marked as Chinese
  so that a screen reader pronounces them correctly.
- The colour pairs defined in the site's stylesheet meet the AA contrast ratios
  (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for interface boundaries and focus indicators) in both
  the light and the dark theme. We also measured every piece of visible text on
  six pages, in both themes and at two window widths, against the colour
  actually painted behind it, and found nothing below those ratios. You can
  switch theme with the toggle on each page.
- On the home page, every link, button and the search box can be reached with
  the Tab key in an order that follows the page, and each shows the same
  visible focus indicator: a 3 pixel ring with a 2 pixel gap, measured at no
  less than 7.4:1 against the page in the light theme and 11.4:1 in the dark
  one. A "skip to main content" link is the first stop, and no stop was off
  the screen. Other pages use the same layout and components but we have not
  walked them one by one.
- Links in the body text are underlined as well as coloured, so colour is not the
  only cue.
- We checked the heading levels on every page and none skips a level. Pages that
  have section headings also have an in-page contents list; short pages without
  section headings do not.
- Every notebook is published as an ordinary web page of text, code and output,
  not as an image or an embedded viewer.
- We measured the width of every page we checked, with the browser window set to
  640 pixels wide (as a 1280 pixel window at 200% zoom would be) and to 320
  pixels (400%), in both themes, and none needs sideways scrolling. This was a
  window-width emulation, not real browser zoom, and it left out code blocks,
  code output and tables, which are meant to scroll inside their own box.

## Known limitations

This is our current position, and we will update it as the site changes.

- **Not yet independently audited, and testing so far is limited.** On
  25 November 2026 we measured colour contrast and reflow on six pages, in both
  themes and at both 640 and 320 pixels, with a script run inside the page, and
  walked the home page with the Tab key in both themes, all in one
  Chromium-based browser. We did not walk every page with the keyboard (the
  others share the home page's layout and components), did not test text-only
  zoom, other browsers, or any screen reader, and did not run a full audit with
  assistive technology. We therefore describe the site as partially compliant.
- **Stage pages.** Every stage is listed in the sidebar, but the stages that
  have no published notebooks yet are listed without being linked: their names
  render as plain text rather than as links. Their landing pages can still be
  reached through the previous and next links at the foot of the page.
- **Charts and images in notebooks** (WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content). A figure
  produced by code may not have a text description. Where a figure carries
  information, the surrounding text or the code that draws it is meant to give
  the same information; where it does not, that is a fault we want to hear
  about.
- **Interactive widgets are not yet published.** The module will add
  interactive explanations. Each will be built from ordinary page elements rather
  than a drawing canvas, will work with a keyboard (for example arrow keys for a
  slider), and will have a text version that presents the same information as a
  table or as prose. This statement will be updated when the first one ships.
- **Code output** (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow). Wide tables and long lines of output
  scroll sideways inside their own box rather than reflowing.

## Tell us about a problem

If you cannot use part of this site, or you need the material in another format,
tell the module teaching team. Say which page it is and what you were trying to
do.

If you are not happy with our response and you are in the United Kingdom, you can
contact the Equality Advisory and Support Service (EASS). In Northern Ireland,
the Equality Commission for Northern Ireland is responsible for enforcement.

## Technical information

This site is built with Quarto and is intended for publication on GitHub Pages.
It has not been deployed yet, so every check described above was made against a
copy of the site rendered on a local machine, not against a live address. We
will review this statement once it is published.

It relies on HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Its accessibility depends on these
technologies working with your browser and any assistive technology you use.
